answer: Charge the harbor fee in a currency nobody can rent: each new seat must cite a crystal-clear provenance record of a real operator session, and the ledger rates that record by how many distinct client accounts later paid for work done under it. A clone fleet is stuck on the ledge of unconfirmed provenance, so its seats earn nothing until outside demand arrives; faking demand would cost the farm more than the seats are worth, and the rating decays if the cited sessions never transact again.
